speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; to help narrow this down, have these symptoms been constant or do they come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) or Vestibular Neuritis. Given the constant nature and lack of positional triggers described, Vestibular Neuritis is more likely. I will request a Dix-Hallpike test to confirm if there are any subtle positional triggers, and order an MRI of the brain to rule out central causes given your age and the sudden onset.
